name: What R-value should my home insulation have?
description: The ideal R-value depends on your climate zone, area insulated, and building codes; higher R-values mean better insulation.

mainEntity.name: What R-value should my home insulation have?

acceptedAnswer.text: The ideal R-value for your home's insulation depends on your climate zone, the specific area being insulated (attic, walls, floor), and local building codes. Higher R-values indicate greater insulating power. For example, attics typically require a higher R-value than walls. In the Alameda and East Bay climate, recommended R-values can range, but a professional assessment will determine the optimal level for your specific home to maximize energy efficiency. This is a crucial decision factor to ensure adequate thermal performance.
acceptedAnswer.description: The ideal R-value depends on your climate zone, area insulated, and building codes; higher R-values mean better insulation.
